senses.gloss: m.(b. h. כְּמָרִים; כָּמַרto guard, cmp. כֹּהֵן. In Syriac כומרא interchanges with כהנא, v. P. Sm. 1757 s. v.) attendant, priest, always used of idolaters.
units: <cite ref="Kiddushin 20b:2">Kidd. 20ᵇ</cite> <he>נעשה כ׳ לע״ז</he> (<cite ref="Arakhin 30b:43">Arakh. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>משרת</he>) became an attendant of an idolatrous temple.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:5:3">Y. Ab. Zar. I, 39ᵈ</cite>.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 35:1">Pesik. R. s. 35</cite> <he>יתרו לא כ׳ וכ׳</he> was not Jethro an idolatrous priest?; a. fr.—Pl. <he>כּוּמָרִים</he>, <he>כּוּמָרִין</he>.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 51b:18">Ab. Zar. 51ᵇ</cite> <he>בטובת כ׳</he> for the benefit of the idolatrous priests, opp. <he>עובדיה</he> worshippers; Y. ib. IV, 43ᵈ bot.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 65">Gen. R. s. 65</cite>, beg.; a. fr.
